column1: # Javanese Latin ⟨e⟩ lexicon — CROSS-SCRIPT TRANSFER (the Punjabi Gurmukhi↔Shahmukhi pattern). Latin ⟨e⟩ conflates
# pepet /ə/ and taling /e/~/ɛ/ — BOTH written ⟨e⟩ and unrecoverable from Latin orthography (no rule; that IS the
# ambiguity). The Aksara Jawa script writes them with distinct signs, so it is more phonemic.
# PROVENANCE: each Aksara word (full kaikki Javanese dump — 2365 Aksara headwords + 149 exact Latin↔Aksara pairs)
# was transliterated to its Latin key (Aksara→Latin is DETERMINISTIC, collapsing pepet/taling→⟨e⟩, exactly the
# ambiguity) and phonemized via our own ⟨e⟩-resolving Aksara front-end; the resolved pronunciation is pinned to the
# Latin key where the Latin default (⟨e⟩→ə) differs. Reliable — the sister SCRIPT (deterministic), not a noisy
# consensus. Kept ONLY the ⟨e⟩-only diffs (a synonym in the kaikki forms field differs in consonants → excluded:
# deling→pring dropped). A single-referee a→ɔ loan-exception layer was mined and DROPPED — it was noisy (the kaikki
# entry kutha→kuʈa contradicts the hand-verified golden kuʈɔ; that tail needs a reliable exception source).
# Overrides the SHIPPED Latin path only; phonemizeWordRules (and the referee eval) bypass it. Numbers bypass it too.
